overview.summary: Novartis has transformed into a focused innovative medicines company post-Sandoz spinoff. Cosentyx (secukinumab) remains their immunology anchor at $6B+, now expanding into hidradenitis suppurativa and axial spondyloarthritis. The company's strategy combines IL-17 franchise depth (Cosentyx + ixekizumab successor planning) with cardiovascular (Entresto/Leqvio), oncology (Kisqali, Pluvicto), and next-gen platforms (radioligand therapy, RNA therapeutics).
keyStrengths: Cosentyx: $6B+ franchise dominating PSO/PsA/axSpA/HS with deep indication portfolio
Radioligand therapy leadership (Pluvicto) — first-mover in precision oncology
Entresto ($7B+) cardiovascular anchor provides cash flow stability
Strong European/Spanish market presence with dedicated derm sales force
overview.threatRationale: Novartis's Cosentyx is the primary competitive threat to Almirall's Ilumetri (tildrakizumab) in psoriasis. Cosentyx's superior efficacy data (PASI 90/100 rates), broader label (PSO + PsA + axSpA + HS), and massive promotional spend make it the incumbent biologic in moderate-to-severe PSO. Additionally, Novartis is developing next-gen IL-17 assets that could further pressure the psoriasis space.
